title: Bine Trees: Enhancing Collective Operations by Optimizing Communication Locality
problem: On large HPC systems with oversubscribed networks (dense internal connections, sparse global links), collective operations generate excessive global-link traffic, creating bottlenecks and reducing performance.
motivation: Communication locality—minimizing traffic on globally constrained links—is critical for performance on systems with hierarchical network topologies. Collective algorithms must be adapted to exploit this locality.
method: Bine trees—structures based on binomial negabinary trees—reorganize collective operations (coordinations where all computers send data) to route messages through local network links rather than scarce global connections, keeping traffic flowing within dense clusters instead of bottlenecking. The authors built eight Bine-based collective operations and evaluated them on four network topologies: Dragonfly, Dragonfly+, oversubscribed fat-tree, and torus.
key_novelty: Bine trees reduce the global-link traffic created by collective operations by up to 33% by routing messages through local connections, while maintaining the design flexibility of binomial trees and butterfly network structures.
contributions: Bine tree family for communication-locality-aware collectives
Implementation of eight Bine-based collective operations
Up to 5x speedups on large-scale supercomputers
Consistent reduction in global-link traffic (up to 33%) across diverse topologies
limitations: Evaluation limited to specific topologies; overhead of topology-aware routing not quantified; applicability to newer network architectures (e.g., Slim Fly) not explored.
